findings.text: Central return path first attempts to dequeue a pending signal and deliver it, otherwise it rewinds or renumbers an interrupted system call and finally restores any saved signal mask when no handler runs.

Interrupted call handling converts restart requests for restart block and no handler cases into an interrupted error, honors the restart flag for interruptible waits, otherwise restores the original call number and steps the instruction pointer back, then clears single step state, builds the handler frame, clears direction resume and trap flags, resets user floating state, and completes setup accounting.

Thirty two bit compat frame creation on sixty four bit kernels requires a user restorer, allocates a frame plus floating area, captures context flags, prepares shadow stack state, then publishes flags link alternate stack pad restorer address processor context and mask under a single user access window, optionally publishes extended signal info, and finally points the stack and instruction pointers at the frame and handler while loading user code and data selectors and handler argument registers.
Observed compat frame ordering groups a signal info record with a user context containing flags link stack pad machine context and mask plus a precode slot, with floating state referenced separately.

Compat signal info conversion builds a thirty two bit external record from the kernel record, refreshes child user and system times for child notifications, and reports a fault if the final copy to user fails.

Sixty four bit synchronous return validates the frame accessibility, loads mask and flags, installs the blocked set, restores alternate stack and processor context, restores shadow stack, returns the restored result, and on any failure reports a bad frame and forces a segmentation fault.

Extended thirty two bit synchronous return follows the same validation and restore order with a smaller stack adjustment and compat alternate stack handling, returning the restored result or forcing a segmentation fault on failure.

Thirty two bit returns inhibit single step on exception return, derive the frame from the stack with different small adjustments for plain and real time variants, install the blocked set from old mask words or extended mask, restore low registers and floating state, and for the real time form also restore the alternate stack, forcing a segmentation fault on any bad frame.

Sixty four bit context restore disables restart handling, copies general and extended registers instruction and stack pointers, forces user privilege on code and stack selectors, merges only the permitted flag bits, disables further syscall checks, repairs the stack selector for old user images unless strict restore is requested in sixty four bit mode, then restores floating state.

Thirty two bit context restore disables restart handling, copies low general registers and pointers, forces user privilege, merges permitted flags, disables syscall checks, reloads segment selectors with privilege fixup either through live reload helpers or direct register writes depending on emulation build, then restores compat floating state.

Both sixty four and thirty two bit context creation publish general registers trap number error code instruction pointer flags selectors stack address floating location old mask and fault address, with sixty four bit builds zeroing segment base selectors and thirty two bit builds capturing live or saved selector values.

User entry invariant forces code and stack selectors to privilege three and repairs selector request levels so null stays null and others gain user privilege, with conditional reload of extra segments only when changed.

Virtual eighty six save enables interrupts before touching user memory, merges virtual interrupt related flags under a mask, writes general registers instruction pointer flags stack and all segment selectors to one of two user structure sizes, then under disabled preemption restores the kernel stack host code selector and task stack tracking, clears the saved stack marker, copies back protected registers, reloads the extra segment, and returns the supplied result code.

Faults while accessing user frames or virtual eighty six structures do not leave partial state: frame builders abort with a fault status, virtual eighty six save logs an alert forces termination with a segmentation fault yet still performs the protected exit sequence, and bad return frames funnel through a common fault reporter.

Alternate stack size validation asserts the caller holds the signal handler lock, and virtual eighty six exit performs stack and selector restoration with preemption disabled after re enabling interrupts for the user copy phase.

Alternate stack acceptance compares the requested size against worst case frame size minus default floating size plus leader permitted user state size, bypassing checks when floating size is static and strict mode is off, otherwise requiring strictly larger size in strict mode or when dynamic user features are permitted.

Restart behavior preserves the original call number in a dedicated field, steps the instruction pointer back by two bytes on restart, and for restart block handling selects either the native restart number or a compat or extended variant preserving the mode bit.

Signal action setup tags actions created through thirty two bit or extended thirty two bit calls with distinct markers, and signal info delivery to thirty two bit users dispatches to the extended variant when in the extended call mode.

Thirty two bit signal code selects between compat and native set info and alternate stack helpers plus syscall numbers through parallel macro sets chosen by emulation build, keeping call sites uniform across builds.
Both word sizes enforce at compile time that every signal info union member starts at the same offset as the common payload and occupies an expected size.

Stop callback ignores the interrupt on the processor recorded as stopping, otherwise disables virtualization for emergency and stops the processor, always reporting handled, with the stopping identifier initially negative and the disable flag initially clear.

Handler entry derives the user frame from the current stack with small word size dependent adjustments, then loads the stack pointer with the frame address, the instruction pointer with the handler address, and the first three argument registers with signal number info pointer and context pointer while installing user selectors.

Bad return frames emit a rate limited message including process identity location frame instruction stack and original call details plus a symbolic address, then force a segmentation fault, while every successful context restore path first forces pending restarts to fail as interrupted.

This lane exposes frame setup and teardown, central signal dispatch and fault reporting, virtual eighty six state save, alternate stack validation, compat signal info copy, and compat action tagging for use by entry and signal layers.
Small helpers read live selector values, force user privilege on selectors, merge flag words under a mask, and prefix log messages with the module name.
